Recommendation: refuse. The coin is down 87% from its 30-minute high, the last 15 minutes show -31% return with net outflow of 5.77 SOL and sell pressure (21.88 SOL sold vs 16.12 bought), and it is only 30.7 minutes old, which puts it in the window where we've lost about 20% per trade. Pool depth is about 31 SOL, so a $20 ticket plus a 1.4-5.1% round trip is a meaningful slice of available liquidity, and exit slippage on a falling coin would likely be worse than the quoted range.

Note the fresh-launch pattern (launch bot present, sell-to-buy ratio above 1 in the first two minutes) also argues against entry. The "ORGANIC" label and the 15% bundle share are not enough to override a confirmed downtrend.

If the desk overrides and insists on a position, the most conservative sizing is $5, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold, but I would not endorse entry. Revisit only if the pool stabilizes, net flow turns positive over several intervals, and the drawdown stops deepening.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying is weak. The strongest points are: the curve looks organic (bundle share 15%, top-3 holders only 7.6%, no airdrop dump seen), 480 curve buyers, and the coin is still alive with 222 non-agent buyers in its first two minutes after graduation.

But the recent flow says demand has already left. Over the last 15 minutes, sellers (69) outnumbered buyers (52), net flow is -5.77 SOL, and the sell-to-buy ratio in the graduation window was 1.13. The price is down 87% from its 30-minute high and 84% over 30 minutes. A launch bot was present, and the pool is thin at 31 SOL.

There is no credible case that real demand will still be here in 30-60 minutes. The organic classification and clean holder distribution are real positives, but they describe how the coin was distributed, not whether anyone wants it now. Buying a coin in an active, sustained sell-off with a momentum signal this negative is the pattern the base rates punish. Recommendation: skip.

The sell-to-buy ratio of 1.13 in the first two minutes after graduation and a launch bot present suggest early buyers have been exiting. With only 30.97 SOL of pool depth, a $20 round trip costing 1.4-5.1% plus impact would need a sharp bounce to pay off, and dead-cat bounces rarely hold. Skip.
